data.name: Alaska
data.summary: Alaska's Rural Health Transformation Program remains in active statewide implementation, led by the Department of Health with oversight from an Advisory Council and broad stakeholder engagement. Program awards are proceeding from formal notifications to grant execution, aligning projects with six core rural health transformation priorities and administrative reviews. Year 2 planning features operational improvements, streamlined applications, enhanced applicant support, and additional funding opportunities, maintaining focus on workforce, access, infrastructure, healthy communities, financial sustainability, and technology modernization. The program tracks a structured portfolio of key initiatives and strategic goals across all rural regions. Current structured plan tracks 20 key initiatives and 26 strategic goals.

data.name: Alabama
data.summary: The Alabama Rural Health Transformation Program (ARHTP), managed by ADECA and guided by the ARHTP Advisory Group, is currently implementing multi-year, statewide initiatives focused on improving rural health access, workforce sustainability, health IT modernization, EMS and trauma systems, mental and maternal health, and cybersecurity. The program operates annual cycles of project funding and workshops, with Year 1 awards complete and Year 2 applications set to reopen. Implementation is coordinated by state agencies and stakeholders, follows a structured plan with eleven core initiatives, and is driven by data analysis and broad input. Current structured plan tracks 12 key initiatives and 7 strategic goals.

data.name: Arkansas
data.summary: Arkansas’s Rural Health Transformation Program is in active implementation, with applications open for initiative funding through HEART, RISE, PACT, and THRIVE. The program targets high-need rural populations, focusing on improving access, population health, telehealth integration, workforce development, and emergency services modernization, guided by ongoing stakeholder input. Behavioral health transition services and community partnership networks remain priority focus areas. Current structured plan tracks 11 key initiatives and 8 strategic goals.

data.name: Arizona
data.summary: The Arizona Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP), administered by AHCCCS, continues active implementation with major grant initiatives projected through at least 2026. RHTP maintains its focus on workforce development, access to care, health system strengthening, and collaborative approaches for rural and Tribal communities. Applicants must attest to fiscal stewardship and the non-supplanting of funds, and the program operates under structured oversight with an implementation plan tracking multiple key initiatives and strategic goals within a defined governance framework. Current structured plan tracks 10 key initiatives and 7 strategic goals.

data.name: California
data.summary: The California Rural Health Transformation (CalRHT) Program is in early implementation, administered by the Department of Health Care Access and Information with CMS oversight. It aims to build a connected and resilient rural health system focused on workforce development, recruitment and retention, technology and EHR modernization, regional collaboration, and community engagement. Current activities include phased grant funding for workforce expansion, technology upgrades, care model improvements, and engagement through Council-led webinars and stakeholder meetings to guide initiatives and monitor progress. Program efforts are guided by a structured plan tracking key initiatives and strategic goals. Current structured plan tracks 12 key initiatives and 12 strategic goals.

data.name: Colorado
data.summary: The Colorado Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) is a federally funded initiative administered by the Department of Health Care Policy and Financing (HCPF) in partnership with CMS, transitioning from program design to statewide implementation for the 2026–2027 grant cycle, supported by technical assistance from the Colorado Rural Health Center (CRHC) across all rural and frontier counties. The program emphasizes workforce development, provider stability, integrated care, health IT modernization, EMS improvements, and readiness for value-based payments, guided by updated eligibility and application requirements. Current efforts focus on measurable outcomes, regional collaboration, stakeholder engagement, and a structured grant review process to ensure completion by September 30, 2027, with grant awards to be announced by the end of September 2026. Current structured plan tracks 26 key initiatives and 14 strategic goals.

data.name: Connecticut
data.summary: Connecticut's Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP), led by the Department of Social Services, is currently implementing projects across four main focus areas: population health outcomes, workforce development, data and technology modernization, and care transformation and stability. The program is underway with active stakeholder engagement—including new Rural Health Advisory Council activities—and emphasizes reducing avoidable hospital utilization, chronic disease management, integration with the state health information exchange, and technology-enabled care models. Current structured plan tracks 10 key initiatives and 10 strategic goals.

data.name: Delaware
data.summary: Delaware’s Rural Health Transformation Program is actively implementing a structured, multi-year strategy, with initial RFPs released for a four-year medical school, expanding school-based health centers in rural Sussex County, developing Food Is Medicine infrastructure, and deploying rural health hubs with mobile health unit networks. The program maintains focus on rural care disparities by prioritizing workforce development, prevention, access, nutrition-integrated care, telehealth, and partnership-driven capacity building. Current efforts track defined initiatives and strategic goals to support measurable outcomes, with additional RFPs planned to advance program objectives. Current structured plan tracks 19 key initiatives and 10 strategic goals.

data.name: Florida
data.summary: Florida's Rural Health Transformation Program, administered by the Agency for Health Care Administration, has awarded the full scope of funding for fiscal year 2026 to hospitals, FQHCs, rural clinics, universities, and community organizations statewide. The program is currently implementing competitive Requests for Applications, with a focus on expanding access, building rural hospital capacity, workforce development, Medicaid value-based purchasing, and infrastructure for value-based payment readiness. Awarded initiatives support expanded rural health care access, provider capacity, and workforce training, with implementation milestones for value-based contracts and health information exchange enrollment. The structured plan continues to track key initiatives and strategic goals. Current structured plan tracks 20 key initiatives and 11 strategic goals.

data.name: Georgia
data.summary: Georgia's Rural Health Transformation Program, under the GREAT Health initiative, is in active multi-year implementation across rural counties, deploying a federally funded value-based care transformation model. Current efforts are focused on technology-driven workforce retention—through initiatives like surgical robotics and telehealth expansion—public health investments such as newborn screening, behavioral health support, consumer engagement, and workforce development via nursing education, GME program expansion, and EMS training. Recent awards and grant cycles demonstrate sustained investment in infrastructure, healthcare education, and innovative care delivery models. The program operates under a structured plan with defined key initiatives and strategic goals. Current structured plan tracks 17 key initiatives and 11 strategic goals.

data.name: Hawaii
data.summary: The Hawaii Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) is in active planning and early implementation, following a major federal award supporting integrated initiatives to strengthen rural health systems statewide. The program prioritizes six core areas, including telehealth, rural infrastructure modernization, workforce pipeline and training, EMS and respite care, and value-based innovation, with planned investments in health IT, EMS upgrades, and provider supports. Initiatives are targeted toward neighbor islands and rural Oʻahu to address access barriers and workforce shortages, with hospital and provider system alignments underway and formal funding opportunities forthcoming. Current structured plan tracks 14 key initiatives and 9 strategic goals.

data.name: Iowa
data.summary: The Iowa Rural Health Transformation Program, administered by state agencies with multi-year federal funding, is currently in pilot and early award phases supporting Critical Access Hospitals and rural healthcare providers. Major focus areas include establishing hub-and-spoke care models, provider partnerships, workforce recruitment via expanded rural residencies, and development of health hubs for cancer and cardiovascular care. The program operates under five main initiatives—Hometown Connections, Combat Cancer, Communities of Care, Health Information Exchange, and EMS Community Care Mobile—with implementation advancing through competitive RFPs and scheduled awards managed via IowaGrants.gov. Progress is measured by structured initiatives and strategic goals, consistent with ongoing RFP issuances and tracking. Current structured plan tracks 12 key initiatives and 10 strategic goals.

data.name: Idaho
data.summary: Idaho's Rural Health Transformation Program remains in its initial implementation phase under the Department of Health and Welfare, with executed contracts and subgrants through 2026. Informed by extensive stakeholder input, the program focuses on workforce recruitment and retention, innovative care models, technology expansion, and infrastructure modernization. Current priorities include rural provider capacity, maternal and behavioral health, chronic disease prevention, cancer screening, cognitive health pathways, and evaluation of outcomes, with structured activities tracked across multiple targeted initiatives and strategic goals. The program's first-year funds have been obligated and contracting for key initiatives is underway. Current structured plan tracks 18 key initiatives and 13 strategic goals.

data.name: Illinois
data.summary: Illinois is currently implementing the Rural Health Transformation Program following federal award approval and allocation of first-year funding. The program, led by the Illinois Department of Healthcare and Family Services, focuses on expanding equitable access and reducing barriers to care in rural areas through initiatives such as hospital transformation, workforce development, technology-enabled care, and maternal and chronic disease priorities. HFS is actively establishing governance structures, issuing NOFOs, advancing regional partnerships, and supporting provider and community-based organization capacity-building, with performance tracked by structured plans with key initiatives and strategic goals. Multi-year activities and substantial stakeholder engagement continue as Illinois builds a resilient rural healthcare delivery ecosystem. Current structured plan tracks 17 key initiatives and 12 strategic goals.

data.name: Indiana
data.summary: Indiana’s Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) is currently active, led by the Indiana Department of Health and Family and Social Services Administration, and emphasizes broad stakeholder engagement with sustained improvement in rural health outcomes. Current major focus areas include care coordination, workforce development, telehealth expansion, technology enhancements, clinical training, and pediatric and obstetric readiness. The structured plan tracks numerous interconnected initiatives and strategic goals, detailing implementation efforts in digital infrastructure, maternal and pediatric readiness, eliminating barriers to care, and regional grants. The program remains in full implementation, strengthening rural health infrastructure and access statewide. Current structured plan tracks 36 key initiatives and 21 strategic goals.

data.name: Kansas
data.summary: The Kansas Rural Health Transformation Program, administered by KDHE in partnership with organizations such as the Kansas Rural Health Innovation Alliance and Healthworks, is actively implementing structured initiatives to improve rural health outcomes, including care model innovation, technology adoption, workforce pipeline development, and targeted pilot programs for dementia care and chronic disease management. Current focus areas include Emerging Technology grants, centralized credentialing, revenue technical support, Community Health Worker and Accountable Food is Medicine projects, workforce development, and interfacility transport improvements. Current structured plan tracks 14 key initiatives and 12 strategic goals.

data.name: Kentucky
data.summary: The Kentucky Rural Health Transformation Program is actively implementing initiatives in community health worker training, EMS transformation, behavioral health crisis response, rural dental access, chronic care (with phased rollout of regional chronic care hubs focused on diabetes and obesity), maternal health, and regional health hub development. Multiple funding opportunities and structured applications are available for health departments, EMS agencies, behavioral health organizations, and educational institutions, with major focus on technology-enabled care and multisector collaboration. Current structured plan tracks 10 key initiatives and 5 strategic goals.

data.name: Louisiana
data.summary: The Louisiana Rural Health Transformation Program, led by the Department of Health and the Office of Rural Health Transformation, is actively implementing its first budget year with a structured plan focused on workforce development, value-based care, healthcare infrastructure, telehealth, interoperability, EMS, and rural health innovation. The program is administering competitive funding opportunities through August 2026, supporting rural clinician recruitment and retention, provider sustainability, care models, Medicaid alternative payment models, technology modernization, capital improvements, and food-as-medicine initiatives. Program governance and stakeholder engagement continue to expand, anchored by an advisory council and cross-sector partner collaboration. Current structured plan tracks 15 key initiatives and 16 strategic goals.

data.name: Massachusetts
data.summary: Massachusetts was awarded $162 million in December 2025 to support rural healthcare transformation. The program's vision is a Commonwealth where rural communities thrive, focusing on access, well-being, and resilient systems. The HCWC State Office of Rural Health leads these efforts with targeted initiatives and partnerships. Current structured plan tracks 8 key initiatives and 3 strategic goals.

data.name: Maryland
data.summary: Maryland's Rural Health Transformation Program, administered by the State Office of Rural Health, is actively implementing a structured plan initiated after its federal award in December 2025 and supported by ongoing federal funding. The program centers on three pillars: rural health workforce transformation, sustainable access and innovative care—including primary care, behavioral health and telehealth expansion—and empowering healthy food choices in state-designated rural areas. Active procurements, competitive subawards, and data-driven projects support continued investments in training, facility upgrades, workforce pathways, and food systems, with community engagement informing strategic goals. Current structured plan tracks 11 key initiatives and 6 strategic goals.

data.name: Maine
data.summary: Maine's Rural Health Transformation Program is a federally funded, multi-year initiative in active implementation, supported by a $190 million CMS award. Guided by five strategic initiatives—population health, workforce, technology and innovation, access, and sustainability—the program currently focuses on electronic medical record modernization, workforce development, hospital financial efficiency, and expanding digital health infrastructure including telehealth and AI tools. Progress is tracked against structured goals and timelines, with ongoing advisory and provider engagement. Current structured plan tracks 12 key initiatives and 7 strategic goals.

data.name: Michigan
data.summary: Michigan’s Rural Health Transformation Program is in its initial implementation phase for FY 2026–2030 after receiving federal CMS approval and award, led by the Michigan Department of Health and Human Services. The program has launched its first round of grant solicitations targeting digital health modernization, Medicaid primary care transformation, workforce expansion, chronic disease management, and cross-agency coordination, with ongoing efforts in regional partnerships, transparent reporting, and collaboration with LEO and an advisory council. Current priorities include workforce capacity, health information technology and telehealth, care coordination, behavioral and chronic disease health, transportation access, digital infrastructure investment, and sustainability for rural providers. Current structured plan tracks 15 key initiatives and 20 strategic goals.

data.name: Minnesota
data.summary: The Minnesota Rural Health Transformation Program, administered by the Department of Health's Office of Rural Health and Primary Care, is actively implementing structured initiatives to support rural and Tribal healthcare, with recent RFPs issued for hospitals, clinics, tribal nations, and clinicians. Current focus areas include workforce retention, clinical training and residency expansion, pediatric and adolescent mental health, provider collaboration, expanded telehealth and health IT access, targeted technical assistance—including a Rural Telehealth Services Center needs assessment—and thorough stakeholder engagement. The program continues to use evidence-based frameworks, tracking progress across multiple key strategic goals and initiatives through 2030. Current structured plan tracks 16 key initiatives and 13 strategic goals.

data.name: Missouri
data.summary: Missouri's Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP), led by MO HealthNet Division and Department of Social Services, remains in the implementation phase, advancing the ToRCH Care model through 27 regional Community Hubs to coordinate clinical and non-clinical services. Current focus areas include home visiting, expanding maternal and behavioral health services, EMS and mobile integrated healthcare collaboration, diagnostics, outpatient and chronic disease management, and rural health infrastructure modernization. Facility upgrades, workforce development—including EMS, MIH-CP, and maternal health—and investments in digital and virtual care infrastructure are actively supported through ongoing grants and structured initiatives. Current structured plan tracks 17 key initiatives and 11 strategic goals.

data.name: Mississippi
data.summary: The Mississippi Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) is in its initial implementation phase, overseen by the Governor’s Office and state agencies, with a third-party administrator coordinating targeted grant initiatives. The program is rolling out efforts focused on workforce expansion, psychiatric emergency services, EMS capacity, telehealth adoption, technology upgrades, and rural provider infrastructure improvements. Current activities emphasize measurable workforce recruitment and retention, behavioral health crisis care, EMS regional organization, and technology modernization. The structured program plan includes multiple initiatives and strategic goals, supported by continuous stakeholder engagement and clear accountability requirements. Current structured plan tracks 15 key initiatives and 12 strategic goals.

data.name: Montana
data.summary: Montana is actively implementing the Rural Health Transformation Program under a five-year structured plan focused on workforce development, sustainable access, innovative care models, community health and prevention, and technology innovation. Administered by the Department of Public Health and Human Services with oversight from Stakeholder Advisory and Center of Excellence councils, the program engages tribal nations, providers, nonprofits, educational institutions, and agencies. Major priorities include statewide deployment of an Emergency Medical Dispatch System, expansion of the Community Health Aide Program to strengthen rural and tribal health services, recruitment support in rural and frontier counties, and ongoing competitive grant and RFP opportunities. Current structured plan tracks 17 key initiatives and 17 strategic goals.

data.name: North Carolina
data.summary: North Carolina's Rural Health Transformation Program is advancing toward implementation, with six regional NC ROOTS Hubs awarded to lead coordination of rural health transformation initiatives across 85 counties. Current focus areas include the integration of primary care, behavioral, and social health services, chronic disease prevention, maternal health, workforce development, provider preparation for value-based care, and digital health innovation. Program activities are organized by NC DHHS in collaboration with state agencies, community stakeholders, and a statewide advisory committee prioritizing transparency and multi-sector engagement. Current structured plan tracks 15 key initiatives and 14 strategic goals.

data.name: North Dakota
data.summary: The North Dakota Rural Health Transformation Program is implementing phased, competitive funding rounds targeting workforce stabilization, preventive care, behavioral health, and health technology modernization in rural and tribal communities. Current focus areas include workforce training and retention, safety net service delivery, telehealth and remote monitoring, and data and infrastructure upgrades designed to support measurable, sustainable improvements in health care access and outcomes. The program emphasizes collaboration and local leadership, with structured grant opportunities tracked across four major pillars and progress monitored against established goals. As of late 2026, most Year 1 funding opportunities have closed, with leadership transition and active review of remaining applications underway. Current structured plan tracks 27 key initiatives and 10 strategic goals.

data.name: Nebraska
data.summary: The Nebraska Rural Health Transformation Program is in its initial implementation stage, launching statewide initiatives beginning in Spring 2026 with rolling funding opportunities for rural providers each year. Primary focus areas remain food as medicine, emergency and behavioral health, workforce acceleration, eHealth, and facility modernization, under active oversight by the Nebraska Department of Health and Human Services with structured input from newly established Health Care Advisory Regions. The program emphasizes technology-enabled solutions, regional care coordination, and targeted rural workforce and access improvements. Current structured plan tracks 18 key initiatives and 24 strategic goals.

data.name: New Hampshire
data.summary: The New Hampshire Rural Health Transformation Program, managed by the Foundation for Healthy Communities and GO-NORTH and funded by CMS for 2026–2030, is in the implementation phase with active contracts and open funding opportunities. The program operates through five regional hubs and focuses on improving rural healthcare access, quality, workforce development, technology adoption, financial sustainability, and the expansion of primary, behavioral, and specialty care. Current activities include tracking key initiatives aligned with population health, primary and behavioral care expansion, school-based oral health, and technology infrastructure, supported by targeted RFPs/RFAs and technical assistance. Current structured plan tracks 26 key initiatives and 15 strategic goals.

data.name: New Jersey
data.summary: The New Jersey Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) is currently implementing a structured portfolio of initiatives to advance technology deployment, prevention, workforce development, and expanded capacity for rural hospitals, community health workers, doula integration, and EMS services. The program operates an updated resource directory linking providers with approved vendors, and issues regular competitive grants focused on telehealth, chronic disease management, maternal health, and emergency medical services. Strategic goals and activities are actively tracked across collaborative phases, with ongoing grant cycles and targeted initiatives addressing infrastructure, workforce development, technology, and innovative care for uninsured and underinsured rural populations. The current phased plan tracks key initiatives and strategic goals, with annual reporting and ongoing implementation throughout the five-year federal award period. Current structured plan tracks 12 key initiatives and 15 strategic goals.

data.name: New Mexico
data.summary: Major focus areas include workforce development, system sustainability, community-based innovation, and improved access to care—including specialty, maternal, behavioral health, and chronic disease services—for rural, frontier, and tribal populations. The program emphasizes enhancing infrastructure, advancing health equity, supporting local solutions, and integrating health data through strategic investments. Current implementation (2026–2030) follows a structured plan with annual performance-based funding, and multiple major procurements are underway or under evaluation for initiatives such as the Administrative Services Organization, Center for Rural Health Sustainability & Innovation, Healthy Horizons, Rooted in New Mexico, Rural Health Innovation Fund, and the Rural Health Data Hub, all supporting statewide transformation goals. Current structured plan tracks 7 key initiatives and 7 strategic goals.

data.name: Nevada
data.summary: The RHTP is administered by the Nevada Health Authority (NVHA) with support from CMS through a federal cooperative agreement. In 2026, the program is actively implementing multiple funding opportunities targeting rural health innovation, workforce recruitment, tribal health systems, provider infrastructure, and improved access to healthcare. Applicants are advised to review RFA documents for eligibility and guidance. Current structured plan tracks 14 key initiatives and 17 strategic goals.

data.name: New York
data.summary: New York's Rural Health Transformation Program is actively implementing a coordinated plan following the November 2025 CMS application and federal award. The program centers on rural community health integration, partnerships, technology-enhanced and AI-supported primary care, telehealth expansion, cybersecurity resilience, and rural workforce development. The state is finalizing contracts and procurements; funding guidance and applications are due July 14, 2026, and contracts operate from September 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027. Current structured plan tracks four main initiatives targeting integrated networks, primary care, workforce development, and cybersecurity for rural providers. Current structured plan tracks 5 key initiatives and 7 strategic goals.

data.name: Ohio
data.summary: The Ohio Rural Health Transformation Program is in active implementation, with recurring competitive solicitations focused on workforce upskilling and retention, pharmacy transformation, chronic disease prevention and management, technical assistance, and expanding school-based and clinically integrated rural health networks. The Ohio Department of Health manages communications and program operations through structured bidders conferences and coordinated timelines. Current major initiatives include rural workforce pipeline development, community health worker integration, EMS and dispatch modernization, and rural health delivery system strengthening, guided by a structured plan tracking key initiatives and strategic goals. As of 2026, implementation includes the launch of the first awarded project to Ohio University for rural workforce development, ongoing multi-partner collaborations, and continued solicitations across several initiative tracks. Current structured plan tracks 15 key initiatives and 7 strategic goals.

data.name: Oklahoma
data.summary: The Oklahoma Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) is actively implementing a federally supported, multi-year initiative to enhance rural health care access, quality, and sustainability statewide. Current efforts focus on expanding EMS and community paramedicine, transportation reimbursement, microgrants for wellness hubs, infrastructure and workforce development, behavioral health integration, and regional collaboration, with engagement from providers, tribal nations, and community partners. As of 2026, the program tracks up to 75 unique initiatives and 14 key projects guided by stakeholder input and ongoing federal support. Current structured plan tracks 18 key initiatives and 11 strategic goals.

data.name: Oregon
data.summary: Oregon’s Rural Health Transformation Program is actively implementing its 2026 plan, distributing Catalyst and Immediate Impact Awards to support 136 rural health projects statewide. Led by the Oregon Health Authority in partnership with CMS, the program advances five statewide initiatives—regional partnerships, healthy communities, workforce capacity, technology and data modernization, and a Tribal Initiative—with priority areas in maternal/child and behavioral health, infrastructure, and workforce stabilization. Regional convenings and collaboratives provide technical assistance and coordination, with Catalyst Awards representing the program’s largest grant round to date. Current structured plan tracks 12 key initiatives and 17 strategic goals.

data.name: Pennsylvania
data.summary: The Pennsylvania Rural Health Transformation Program is currently active, providing direct funding to rural healthcare providers and facilities for supplies and equipment to stabilize and enhance rural health access, with an emphasis on non-capital projects. Major focus areas include technology modernization, behavioral health, EMS, maternal health, aging access, and workforce development, with current implementation through the Rapid Response Stabilization Program and per-location award caps set for 2026 funding rounds. Funding is administered via coordinated state mechanisms with defined eligibility and regional distribution criteria, and applicants must address one of six targeted RHTP initiatives. Application windows and spending deadlines are currently set through July 2027. Current structured plan tracks 14 key initiatives and 12 strategic goals.

data.name: Rhode Island
data.summary: Rhode Island is implementing the Rural Health Transformation Program across rural towns and the Narragansett Indian Tribe, coordinated by EOHHS and RIDOH with guidance from the Rural Stakeholder Advisory Council. Developed with broad stakeholder input and federal funding through 2030, the program focuses on expanding access—including innovative care models and community health networks—strengthening the healthcare workforce, digital modernization, and health equity. The structured plan monitors multiple initiatives and goals through ongoing community-informed implementation and formal oversight, with current emphasis on workforce development and technology integration. Current structured plan tracks 23 key initiatives and 8 strategic goals.

data.name: South Carolina
data.summary: The South Carolina Rural Health Transformation Program is currently offering infrastructure and capacity-building grants through four targeted initiatives: Connections to Care, Wellness Within Reach, Leveling Up, and Shoring Up to Sustainability. The program emphasizes expanding digital infrastructure, scaling care delivery innovations, supporting workforce development, and strengthening behavioral and maternal health services in rural communities, with applications due June 1, 2026. Implementation is underway, as subrecipient agreements are being distributed and oversight responsibilities established, aligned to CMS strategic goals and federal regulations. Current structured plan tracks 11 key initiatives and 9 strategic goals.

data.name: South Dakota
data.summary: The South Dakota Rural Health Transformation Program is actively implementing its fiscal year 2026 plan, emphasizing digital health modernization, community health worker and workforce recruitment and retention (including maternal health training), EMS advancement, and sustainable systems transformation. The Department of Health administers structured grant and contract programs supporting behavioral health, chronic disease management—including remote monitoring in schools—, infrastructure, and Medicaid Primary Accountable Care Transformation through formal RFP processes and provider technical assistance. Current structured plan tracks 31 key initiatives and 12 strategic goals.

data.name: Tennessee
data.summary: The Tennessee Rural Health Transformation Program is under structured, active implementation, with initial grants awarded to rural providers to enhance healthcare access and quality. Competitive solicitations focus on innovation catalysts, technology solutions, mobile app development for maternal and child health, patient navigation, rural transportation, and community health worker infrastructure, administered under the Rural Healthcare Access Modernization Program (RAMP). The program advances a locally-led model, modernized infrastructure, and improved outcomes for mothers, children, and older adults, with a phased schedule of RFP and RFA releases for community organizations and providers. Current efforts track multiple strategic initiatives and goals across rural regions. Current structured plan tracks 19 key initiatives and 15 strategic goals.

data.name: Texas
data.summary: The Texas Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP), administered by HHSC as Rural Texas Strong, is currently focused on improving rural healthcare capacity through workforce development, telehealth and technology expansion, innovative service delivery, infrastructure upgrades, and support for rural hospitals and providers. The program is actively implementing targeted initiatives and grant opportunities, including rural hospital improvement and labor and delivery support grants, guided by structured plans with ongoing stakeholder engagement. Major initiatives and strategic goals are outlined in the Rural Texas Strong plan, with implementation involving collaboration with local leaders and residents. Current structured plan tracks 26 key initiatives and 19 strategic goals.

data.name: Federal
data.summary: The Federal Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP), established under Public Law 119-21, provides $50 billion in federal support to all 50 states from FY2026 to FY2030 to drive rural health system transformation. Currently in its application and early implementation phase, the program focuses on evidence-based interventions, innovative care models, technology adoption, workforce recruitment and retention, and behavioral health. States must use funds for at least three approved purposes, submit comprehensive transformation plans, demonstrate measurable progress, and comply with annual reporting. Current implementation features structured planning across multiple strategic priorities relevant to rural health care challenges. Current structured plan tracks 14 key initiatives and 18 strategic goals.

data.name: Utah
data.summary: Utah's Rural Health Transformation Program, overseen by the Utah Department of Health and Human Services, is in early implementation with secured federal CMS support through 2030. Ongoing activities include funding opportunities, public stakeholder events, and phased program rollouts tracked by defined initiatives and goals. Program design was guided by extensive stakeholder engagement and aligns with both state and federal priorities. Current structured plan tracks 8 key initiatives and 5 strategic goals.

data.name: Virginia
data.summary: Virginia’s Rural Health Transformation Program is a statewide initiative addressing rural health care access, workforce shortages, and chronic disease through interconnected efforts in workforce development, technology modernization, provider productivity, flexible care models, and chronic disease prevention. As of 2026, the program is actively administering multiple competitive funding opportunities for rural providers, supporting EHR modernization, provider recruitment, remote monitoring, workforce training, and innovative maternal health and community paramedicine models. Implementation is coordinated by the VHHA Foundation and DMAS, in partnership with the Virginia Health Care Foundation and the Virginia Department of Health, under a multi-year plan shaped by extensive stakeholder engagement and collaboration. The current phase emphasizes ongoing tracking of targeted sub-initiatives and strategic goals, with several RFAs presently open and awards expected throughout fall 2026. Current structured plan tracks 19 key initiatives and 8 strategic goals.

data.name: Vermont
data.summary: Vermont's Rural Health Transformation Program, funded by CMS and administered by the Agency of Human Services, has completed Year 1 funding cycles and is preparing for Year 2 opportunities. The program advances 35 activities within five strategic initiatives focused on strengthening the rural workforce, improving timely care access, leveraging innovation, and enhancing quality and cost-effectiveness for underserved and high-need populations. Current implementation includes executed agreements targeting facility improvements, workforce development, health IT, and clinical transformation, with all Year 1 RFP opportunities now closed and Year 2 opportunities forthcoming. Current structured plan tracks 18 key initiatives and 12 strategic goals.

data.name: Washington
data.summary: Washington is actively implementing the Rural Health Transformation Program through the Health Care Authority and state partner agencies, focusing on six strategic initiatives addressing rural hospital innovation, workforce development, technology adoption, behavioral health, community-based care, and Native family health. The program supports collaborative efforts with sub-awardees statewide to advance rural health access and infrastructure, with current activities including program design, competitive awards, and regular updates through webinars. Current structured plan tracks 21 key initiatives and 16 strategic goals.

data.name: Wisconsin
data.summary: The Wisconsin Rural Health Transformation Program is actively implementing a multi-year, CMS-funded portfolio led by the Department of Health Services, with structured oversight including quarterly External Advisory Council reviews. The program comprises over 29 projects across 16 state agencies and centers on strengthening the rural healthcare workforce, advancing digital infrastructure, and improving care coordination through broad partnerships with educational, public health, and tribal organizations. Current management includes regular evaluation, adaptive project guidance, and targeted grant opportunities, with workforce efforts overseen by the Department of Workforce Development and the Wisconsin Office of Rural Health serving as external evaluators and communications liaisons. Current structured plan tracks 10 key initiatives and 9 strategic goals.

data.name: West Virginia
data.summary: West Virginia's Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) is in active implementation, awarding funds for EMS-driven models, mobile-integrated health care, PACE-aligned care for older adults, and expanding worksite clinic and employer-based health services. Recent awards and open solicitations focus on strengthening the healthcare and nursing workforce, expanding transportation, nutrition, prevention programs, virtual care, and the adoption of health IT and data exchange infrastructure. The program continues to track multiple initiatives and strategic goals, with awarded implementation funding and ongoing grant releases supporting projects across care access, workforce, care coordination, prevention, and statewide data integration. Current structured plan tracks 24 key initiatives and 14 strategic goals.
